title: Dont Allow Negative Life Challenges to Become a Part of Your Self-Identity
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece warns against letting a major personal setback — divorce, illness, financial hardship — become fused with a leader's self-identity long after the event itself has passed. It describes how internalizing misfortune produces a running set of self-limiting narratives that leak into how a leader shows up for others. The article distinguishes learning from a setback from letting it define a person permanently, arguing the two are easily conflated. It ends on an empowering note: people retain agency to actively separate the struggle from their ongoing identity.
points: Long personal setbacks are easy to internalize into a person's ongoing self-identity.
Once fused with identity, setbacks generate ready-made excuses that limit how a leader shows up.
Co-mingling misfortune and identity undermines a leader's credibility and confidence.
Those around a struggling leader eventually just accept the negative narrative as who the person has become.
The article insists people retain the choice to separate a past struggle from their future identity.
quotes: By internalizing the misfortune and incorporating it into their understanding of themselves, leaders begin to meld who they are with what they went through.
In essence, they accommodate the setback, allowing it to create a slew of ready-made excuses for why they overreact or avoid many situations.
Leaders who co-mingle misfortune and self-identity undermine their own credibility to lead others.
Nothing happens to anyone that they can’t actively engage to change.
People who depend on leaders for their objectivity, compassion, and wisdom deserve the best version, the one without historical baggage.
